# About local customer optimisation within Performance Max campaign for shop goals

Local customer optimisation is a feature within Performance Max campaigns for shop goals that allows you to prioritise reaching potential customers who are close to or interested in your business area and ready to take action immediately, such as visit or contact.

This campaign feature is intended to reach potential customers at the most critical moment when they are actively navigating, trip planning or searching for locations on Google Maps, Waze or Google Search for a service in a specific area of interest.

Learn more [about Performance Max for shop goals](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/12971048).

**Note:** Local customer optimisation is not compatible with online campaign goals and Performance Max campaigns with products from Merchant Center.

**On this page**

*   [Benefits of local customer optimisation](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/17198659?hl=en-GB#benefits)
*   [Steps to enable local customer optimisation toggle](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/17198659?hl=en-GB#stepstoenable)
*   [Updating your conversion goal](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/17198659?hl=en-GB#updating)

## Benefits of local customer optimisation

Local customer optimisation may help businesses with physical locations increase their local visibility and offers the following additional benefits:

*   **Capture ready-to-act customers:** Reach users who are ready to take actions immediately as they plan routes, search for services or travel near your business location with immediate intent to act.
*   **Targeted local reach:** Target users near your business area by directing campaign budgets to locally tailored ads on channels such as Google Maps, Waze and local formats on Google Search.

* * *

## Steps to enable local customer optimisation

### Create a new Performance Max for shop goals campaign with local customer optimisation toggle

When you create a Performance Max campaign optimising only to offline goals, the local customer optimisation toggle will be available to turn on this feature

1.  Go to [**Campaigns**](http://ads.google.com/aw/campaigns) within the **Campaigns** menu ![Campaigns icon](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/PYU3UjHzepAdY-dWS9ObIzq9WgLGS0SZeJS1hQ0Be3fxCIUQZaWCrR4HoYqriXSEbQ=w40).
2.  Select + **New campaign**.
3.  Choose your campaign objective as **Local shop visits and promotions**, then select **Performance Max** as the campaign type.
4.  Confirm the conversion goals, such as shop visits, shop sales, contacts (Google-hosted) or directions (Google-hosted) for shop goals for your campaign.
5.  You'll find a 'Local customer optimisation' panel with a toggle to turn on the feature.
6.  Select your business locations to target, either from your Business Profile account or your linked location or affiliate location assets.
7.  If your account is linked to a Merchant Center account, deselect 'Advertiser products from a Merchant Center account' as local customer optimisation is not compatible with Performance Max campaigns with products from Merchant Center.
8.  Select **Continue**.

### Manage local customer optimisation in an existing Performance Max for shop goals campaign

Steps to enable local customer optimisation in an existing Performance Max for shop goals campaign.

1.  Go to [**Campaigns**](http://ads.google.com/aw/campaigns) within the **Campaigns** menu ![Campaigns icon](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/PYU3UjHzepAdY-dWS9ObIzq9WgLGS0SZeJS1hQ0Be3fxCIUQZaWCrR4HoYqriXSEbQ=w40).
2.  Select the campaign that you want to edit.
    *   **Note:** If the selected campaign is advertising products from a Merchant Center account, it will not be compatible with local customer optimisation even if the toggle is turned on. Instead, consider selecting a different campaign or creating a new one.
3.  Go to the 'Budget and bidding optimisation' section on the 'Settings' page.
4.  You can turn on the feature under the new setting **Local customer optimisation** panel.

## PERFORMANCE MAX FOR A LOCAL BUSINESS

*   Post author:[admin](https://biznex.app/blogs/author/admin/ "Posts by admin")
*   Post published:October 19, 2026
*   Post category:[Social Media Marketing](https://biznex.app/blogs/category/social-media-marketing/)
*   Post comments:[0 Comments](https://biznex.app/blogs/blogs-performance-max-for-local-business/#respond)

## Performance Max for a Local Business: Is It Worth It?

**Quick answer:** Performance Max (PMax) is a Google Ads campaign type that serves ads across Google’s channels, including Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and Maps, from one campaign. Performance Max for a local business can work if you have reliable conversion data and a budget that supports several weeks of learning. With very small budgets or few conversions, a Search campaign usually gives more control.

Performance Max is the campaign type Google pushes hardest, and many local business owners are told to switch to it. Is Performance Max for a local business a good idea, or a way to spend more with less control? Here’s what it is, what it needs, and seven checks before you start.

### What Performance Max Is

PMax is a goal-driven campaign that uses automation to serve ads across Google’s inventory (Digital Marketing Knight). You supply the goal, conversion tracking, text, images and videos, plus optional audience signals. Google decides where each ad appears, to whom, and at what bid.

### What Performance Max for a Local Business Can Do

*   **Local goals:** Google offers a “Local Store Visits and Promotions” objective, with conversion goals such as store visits and directions (AdNabu).
*   **Google Maps and Business Profile:** local-focused PMax can use your Business Profile and location information to drive visits (Digital Marketing Knight).
*   **Reporting:** Google’s channel performance report includes offline conversions such as local actions, store visits and store sales (Google Ads Help). You can read it on [Google’s help page](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16260130).

One caution. Store visits and store sales in PMax are modeled conversions, and Google recommends store goals only for accounts eligible for store visits (AdNabu). Small businesses often rely on calls or direction clicks instead.

### What It Needs to Work

*   **Conversion volume:** sources differ. One says roughly 20 to 30 conversions a month per campaign (Store Growers), another suggests 15 to 50 a month as a rule of thumb (Digital Marketing Knight), and another says 50 or more helps campaigns exit learning faster (Black Propeller).
*   **Learning time:** estimates range from 6 days to 6 weeks (SEOQuick) and 4 to 6 weeks (George Tsiros). Plan for several weeks.
*   **A budget that supports learning:** one guide suggests about 10 times your target cost per conversion per day (Digital Marketing Knight). Another says to avoid PMax under roughly $1,000 a month in the e-commerce context (Store Growers).

Our reading, which is an inference and not a Google rule: if your budget can’t buy about 20 to 30 real leads a month, PMax will struggle to learn.

### The Risks of Performance Max for a Local Business

*   **Less control.** You can’t pick placements the way you can with Search. Google has added levers, including campaign-level negative keywords, brand exclusions and the channel performance report (Dataslayer; SEOQuick).
*   **Brand cannibalisation.** Without brand exclusions, PMax can target your brand terms, claim the conversions and report inflated results while your Search campaign bids on the same people (George Tsiros).
*   **Resetting the learning.** Most accounts reporting poor results made structural changes in weeks two to three, which reset learning (George Tsiros).
*   **Junk leads.** PMax optimises for the conversions you define. If form fills include spam, it learns from spam. Count only real enquiries, such as calls above a set length or qualified forms.

### Performance Max vs Search for a Small Local Business

*   **Search campaigns:** you choose keywords, see search terms and control budget by campaign. Best for small budgets.
*   **Performance Max:** more reach, more automation and more channels. Best when conversion data is strong.
*   **Both together:** keep your branded Search campaign running and apply brand exclusions to PMax (Dataslayer; Black Propeller).

Our guide on [why Google Ads get clicks but no leads](https://biznex.app/blogs/google-ads-clicks-but-no-leads/) explains the problems that apply to either type.

### 7 Checks Before You Start

1.  **Conversions are real:** tracking works, and spam is excluded.
2.  **Volume:** you can reach about 20 to 30 conversions a month.
3.  **Budget:** you can fund 4 to 6 weeks without cutting it.
4.  **Assets:** you have good photos, short videos and several headlines. Google lets you write up to 15 headlines of 30 characters.
5.  **Business Profile:** it’s linked, complete and accurate.
6.  **Brand exclusions:** set before launch, with a separate branded Search campaign.
7.  **A patience plan:** no major changes for the first few weeks.

### A Local Example

A clinic in Borivali East that gets 5 or 6 enquiries a month from Google Ads probably doesn’t have enough data for PMax. A Search campaign for its main services, plus a complete Business Profile, is the better start. A multi-branch retailer with 40 or more enquiries a month is a stronger fit.

### When to Skip It

*   Your budget is very small.
*   You have fewer than about 15 reliable conversions a month.
*   You can’t stop brand terms leaking in.
*   You need strict control over where ads show.

### Need Help Deciding?

Our [performance marketing](https://biznex.app/lead-generation.php) team can review your account, tracking and budget before you commit.

### FAQs

**What is Performance Max?**  
A Google Ads campaign type that serves ads across Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and Maps from one campaign.

**Is Performance Max good for small local businesses?**  
It can be, if you have reliable conversion data and enough budget. Otherwise Search campaigns usually give more control.

**How much budget does it need?**  
Guidance varies. One suggests about 10 times your target cost per conversion per day. Check your own cost per lead before deciding.

**How long does the learning period last?**  
Sources range from 6 days to 6 weeks. Plan for 4 to 6 weeks and avoid big changes.

**Does PMax replace Search campaigns?**  
Not necessarily. Many advertisers keep a separate branded Search campaign and use brand exclusions.

**Can I see where my PMax ads ran?**  
Yes. Google’s channel performance report shows results by channel.
